module_title: Foundations and Constitutional Basis of the Budget
introduction: At this beginner level, we will define the budget, look at its constitutional roots, and understand the two basic pillars of government finance: Receipts and Expenditure.

core_concepts.title: Annual Financial Statement (Article 112)
core_concepts.description: The word 'Budget' is not mentioned anywhere in the Constitution of India. Instead, Article 112 refers to it as the 'Annual Financial Statement'. It is an estimate of the government's receipts and expenditure for a financial year (April 1 to March 31).

core_concepts.title: The Two Main Pillars
core_concepts.description:
1. Budget Receipts: All the money coming into the government's pockets from various sources. 
2. Budget Expenditure: All the money the government plans to spend on different sectors.

core_concepts.title: Types of Budgets
core_concepts.description:
1. Balanced Budget: Estimated Receipts = Estimated Expenditure. 
2. Surplus Budget: Receipts > Expenditure. 
3. Deficit Budget: Expenditure > Receipts (This is the most common form for developing nations like India).

important_entities.name: Department of Economic Affairs
important_entities.significance: Within the Ministry of Finance, the 'Budget Division' of the Department of Economic Affairs is the core unit responsible for preparing the Union Budget every year.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam question asks: 'In which Article is the term Budget defined?' The answer is: Nowhere. The Constitution only uses the term 'Annual Financial Statement'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The word comes from the French 'Bougette', meaning a small leather bag. Historically, the Finance Minister carried the budget documents in a leather briefcase.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize Article 112. It is a staple question for SSC, Railways, and State PSC exams.
